item.title: Red Sox ride fast start into rematch vs. Rays
item.description: Boston Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy knows his team has figured out the Tampa Bay Rays pretty well this season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Boston Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy knows his team has figured out the Tampa Bay Rays pretty well this season. That said, the Red Sox (84-70) still can learn more about the Rays (93-60) when the teams meet Saturday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Fla. "At this point with (the Rays), we've played them enough already," Tracy said. "We have a pretty good understanding of them, (and) they have a pretty good understanding of us. But you could always pick up more stuff." In Friday's series opener, the Red Sox scored four runs over the first three innings and won 4-2 to snap Tampa Bay's six-game winning streak and improve to 6-5 this season vs. the Rays. Boston currently holds the second wild-card position in the American League but is dealing with several injuries. "We have guys beat up that aren't here, and the hope is we get people healthy, and the roster could look even different a week from now than it does right now," Tracy said. Boston's Willson Contreras is day-to-day after getting hit on the hand, while closer Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) has been unavailable the past two contests. Right-hander Tanner Houck (Tommy John surgery in 2025) and lefty Garrett Crochet (left shoulder inflammation) have advanced in their rehab assignments. Boston left-hander Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02 ERA) is expected to make his 26th start on Saturday and will try to record his sixth consecutive win. Tolle is 1-0 with an 0.75 ERA over 12 innings in his last two starts, allowing one run on eight hits while striking out 19 with a walk. He is 0-2 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts and one relief outing against Tampa Bay, which already has clinched a playoff berth. Whatever Rays pitching coach Kyle Snyder and the rest of the staff have done with trade-deadline acquisition Freddy Peralta certainly has been a success. Acquired by the club from the New York Mets for three prospects on Aug. 2, Peralta (9-11, 4.67 ERA) -- a right-hander who will start for the Rays on Saturday -- arrived from the Big Apple as a lesser version of what he was during his two All-Star seasons with the Milwaukee Brewers. He was 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA with the Mets, but the work was immediately put in by the Rays to adjust Peralta to where he was when he was a 17-game winner with a sub-3.00 ERA last season. "For some reason, when I got here, when I sat here with Kyle and (bullpen coach Jorge Moncada) and (manager Kevin Cash), they told me, like, 'You're gonna do what you want to do here, and we are going to help you to do it,'" Peralta said. "And we know what you need to do to make those adjustments. We just put everything on the table. I just followed all the instructions, and it's what I am right now." With the Rays, Peralta is 4-2 with a 3.86 ERA in eight starts, but his past four outings have been gems. He has pitched 23 innings and has allowed just two runs on 10 hits, with 17 strikeouts, four walks and an 0.78 ERA in that span. "Fastball Freddy," who is using his changeup much more with the Rays, is 0-2 with a 5.40 ERA in three career starts against Boston. Peralta allowed two runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings in a 4-0 loss at Boston on July 11 while with the Mets. --Field Level Media

item.title: Japan come from behind to beat Fiji and win Pacific Nations Cup
item.description: Japan pulled off an upset 20-15 victory over Fiji on Saturday to win the Pacific Nations Cup for the first time in seven years, outrunning and overpowering the islanders as they overturned the form book.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan pulled off an upset 20-15 victory over Fiji on Saturday to win the Pacific Nations Cup for the first time in seven years, outrunning and overpowering the islanders as they overturned the form book. It was Japan’s fourth win in the competition, which this year also included Canada and the United States, and dethroned Fiji who had won six of the last eight editions. Japan’s three tries at a capacity Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium in Tokyo all came from mauls, with Mamoru Harada, Ben Gunter and substitute Samisoni Tua going over, while Sam Greene added a conversion and penalty. Fiji, ranked ninth in world rugby to Japan’s 12th spot, scored two tries through Virimi Vakatawa and captain Tevita Ikanivere, with Caleb Muntz adding a conversion and Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula a penalty. Japan’s superior fitness allowed them to play a quick game that tired out the Fijians, who initially looked as if they would prove too physically powerful for their hosts. Vakatawa’s power saw him drive over the line in the 10th minute for the first try of the match despite four Japanese defenders trying to stop him. The 34-year-old former France international was making his second appearance for Fiji after switching his allegiance. Harada had Japan’s first try from a lineout maul in the 22nd minute when Fiji were down to 14 men after a yellow card for prop Mesake Doge, but the favourites went 12-10 ahead at the break after a short pass at the lineout caught out the Japanese defence and saw Ikanivere sprint away to score. Japan dominated the second-half exchanges with Fiji tiring quickly and the hosts had several rolling mauls that Fiji managed to hold off but eventually broke through when Gunter forced his way over in the 57th minute. Armstrong-Ravula’s penalty for Fiji levelled matters at 15-15 with 15 minutes to go, but another maul allowed Tua to score the match-winning try in a major triumph for Japan.

item.title: Reportan humo cerca del aeropuerto de Riad tras alertas en Arabia Saudita
item.description: Una gran columna de humo pudo verse el sábado cerca del principal aeropuerto de Riad, después de que se escucharon explosiones y Arabia Saudita emitió alertas durante la noche advirtiendo de un posible peligro en los alrededores de la capital, en el contexto de una escalada de ataques del grupo hutí de Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una gran columna de humo pudo verse el sábado cerca del principal aeropuerto de Riad, después de que se escucharon explosiones y Arabia Saudita emitió alertas durante la noche advirtiendo de un posible peligro en los alrededores de la capital, en el contexto de una escalada de ataques del grupo hutí de Yemen. Las imágenes de vídeo y las fotografías de Reuters mostraban una enorme columna de humo negro elevándose en la zona, con la autopista del aeropuerto, el edificio principal de la terminal y otras instalaciones en primer plano. No hubo comentarios inmediatos de la oficina de prensa del Gobierno saudita en respuesta a las preguntas de Reuters sobre el humo y las alertas nocturnas. La defensa civil saudita envió durante la noche alertas por teléfono sobre un posible peligro en Riad y en la ciudad de Al-Kharj, al este de la capital, antes de dar el "fin de alarma" el sábado por la mañana. Un periodista de Reuters en la zona de Olaya, en Riad, escuchó explosiones antes del "fin de alarma". Si bien este año hubo algunas alertas en Riad tras el inicio de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, estas fueron las primeras desde que comenzó la escalada con los hutíes en julio. Los hutíes, que controlan las zonas más pobladas de Yemen y gran parte del norte, han estado lanzando ataques contra Arabia Saudita desde que declararon un bloqueo naval contra Riad en julio, con ataques dirigidos contra buques sauditas en el mar Rojo.

item.title: Phillies turn to improving Andrew Painter in clash vs. Mets
item.description: Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Nolan McLean are providing the New York Mets hope that they eventually will be part of a rotation for a playoff contender.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Nolan McLean are providing the New York Mets hope that they eventually will be part of a rotation for a playoff contender. The Philadelphia Phillies need rookie Andrew Painter to continue proving that now. Painter will take the mound for the Phillies on Saturday afternoon when they visit the Mets in the third contest of a four-game series between the National League East rivals. Painter (3-9, 5.54 ERA) will oppose Scott (4-5, 3.76) in a battle of right-handers. The Phillies missed a chance to take over sole possession of the top wild-card spot in the NL on Friday night, when Thornton and two relievers combined on a six-hitter in the Mets' 6-3 win. The Phillies, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres are tied for the NL's three wild-card spots at 85-69. The Cubs lost to the Cincinnati Reds 6-4 before the Padres created the three-way tie hours later with an 8-2 win over the Miami Marlins. The Arizona Diamondbacks reside five games behind the Phillies, Cubs and Padres. The importance of Painter was further magnified Friday, when Philadelphia fell to 0-2 in bullpen games necessitated by the absence of left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder, 15-day injured list). The All-Star was scratched from his scheduled start against the Atlanta Braves last Saturday, when the Phillies used six pitchers as the Braves rolled to a 12-2 win. On Friday, opener Tim Mayza got just one out and allowed three runs while pitching in Luzardo's spot. The Phillies' bullpen also is being taxed by injury and ineffectiveness. Right-hander Jonathan Bowlan departed Thursday's game vs. the Mets with a tight right groin. On Friday, Orion Kerkering gave up Juan Soto's three-run blast in the sixth inning -- the second homer surrendered by Kerkering in his last three outings, during which he has a 13.50 ERA. "Anybody that gives up runs, when things aren't going good, your confidence is not sky high like when you're getting all your outs and everything's going smoothly," Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. "But we've got to get past that at this point." Painter is 2-1 with a 3.58 ERA in nine starts since being recalled from Triple-A Lehigh Valley on July 31. He didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Sunday, when he gave up one run over five innings as the Phillies beat the Braves 9-4. He has yet to face the Mets in his career. The Mets (70-84) have been under .500 since April and officially were eliminated from playoff contention earlier this week. But McLean and Thornton continued to provide optimism for 2027 by combining to allow just three runs over 12 innings in the first two games of the series. McLean took the hard-luck loss Thursday, when he gave up one run in six innings in the Phillies' 3-0 win. Thornton, McLean and Scott have a combined 3.40 ERA in 66 starts. Thornton and McLean are rookies while Scott is in his second big-league season after Tommy John surgery cut his 2024 campaign short. "I think you have to train like you've never won anything and compete like you've never lost," Mets interim manager Andy Green said Friday night about Thornton. "I think you have to live in that space constantly." Scott took the defeat Sunday after allowing two runs over six innings in the Mets' 2-0 loss to the New York Yankees. He is 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in two career starts against the Phillies. --Field Level Media

item.title: La France prévoit pour 2026 un déficit de 5,4% et une dette publique à 119,3% du PIB - ministère
item.description: La dette publique de la France devrait atteindre 119,3% du produit intérieur brut (PIB) cette année et pourrait grimper à 121,7% en 2027, a indiqué samedi le ministère de l'Economie et des Finances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La dette publique de la France devrait atteindre 119,3% du produit intérieur brut (PIB) cette année et pourrait grimper à 121,7% en 2027, a indiqué samedi le ministère de l'Economie et des Finances. Concernant le déficit budgétaire, le ministère dit tabler sur 5,4% du PIB en 2026 et 5,0% en 2027. En 2025, le ratio dette/PIB de la France était de 115,7%. Ces chiffres ont été communiqués au Haut Conseil des finances publiques, l'organisme chargé d'évaluer les prévisions de recettes et de dépenses, dans le projet de budget du gouvernement.

item.title: With playoff hopes flickering, Orioles square off with Brewers again
item.description: There's no sugar-coating the results for the Baltimore Orioles with eight games left in the regular season.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: There's no sugar-coating the results for the Baltimore Orioles with eight games left in the regular season. They stand three games out of the final wild-card spot in the American League and would need to leapfrog three teams to land in the postseason. So they'll try to wipe away the painful result from Friday night in advance of the second game of the three-game series with the visiting Milwaukee Brewers on Saturday afternoon. The Brewers claimed the series opener Friday with a 6-5, 10-inning escape. The Orioles came back from deficits of 3-0 and 5-3 to forge ties, only to lose in the first extra frame. "Losing right now is tough," Baltimore infielder Coby Mayo said. "Obviously, we did a great job rallying back, and you're going to have those games where you rally back and lose. You're going to have the games where you rally back and win." Brewers manager Pat Murphy lauded his team. "We did some good things," he said. "We were fortunate things worked out." Milwaukee (96-58) has baseball's best record and leads the Los Angeles Dodgers by two games in the race for the top seed in the NL playoffs. The Orioles (75-79) had a three-game winning streak snapped even after scoring two runs in the bottom of the ninth to extend Friday's game. "Our guys have shown the resiliency all year and coming back," manager Craig Albernaz said. "We have numerous comebacks and keep on clawing, fighting back. But also we know where we're at right now. We've got to win as many games as we can is an understatement." Murphy has become a fan of the Orioles' energy under Albernaz. "I don't know what place they're in or what place they are in the standings," Murphy said. "But to have those guys playing the way he's got those guys playing and the commitment and the way the fans are into the game, they're playing like a first-place team." Left-hander Robert Gasser (4-5, 4.30 ERA) will start for the Brewers on Saturday. He has a 2.57 ERA in three outings this month and gave up one run in five innings Sunday in his team's 4-3 loss to the Cincinnati Reds. He does not have a decision this month. Gasser has never faced the Orioles in parts of three big-league seasons. Left-hander Trevor Rogers (10-10, 4.22 ERA) will start for the Orioles. He took an 8-1 loss Sunday when he allowed four runs in six innings vs. the Toronto Blue Jays. That followed two strong outings earlier in the month when he gave up a total of three runs covering 14 innings. Rogers has been the winning pitcher in his past three starts at home. In five career starts vs. the Brewers, he's 4-0 with a 2.84 ERA. The Orioles are juggling bullpen possibilities, particularly with right-hander Felix Bautista joining the team in Baltimore at the beginning of the series. It's unclear if he'll be placed on the active roster this weekend, though he has completed an injury rehabilitation assignment in the minor leagues as he works his way back from surgery in August of last season to repair a torn rotator cuff and a torn labrum. Many of the roster decisions are bound to depend on Baltimore's status in the playoff chase. "There's a lot of factors that go into play; that's one of them," Albernaz said. "We try to factor in everything when we make a decision, but more importantly, it's where the player (is) at and how they are feeling. We don't want to force them into anything that they're not comfortable with or physically comfortable with." The Orioles will honor former first baseman/outfielder Trey Mancini (2016-22) before the game. He'll sign a one-day contract with the team to officially retire as an Oriole. Mancini, 34, played in 701 games for Baltimore, batting .270 with 117 homers and 350 RBIs. He played in five games for the Los Angeles Angels this season, hitting .308 with no homers and four RBIs. --Field Level Media

item.title: White Sox eager for bounce-back effort vs. Tigers
item.description: After watching a six-run lead disappear, the Chicago White Sox have little time to regroup in a tightening American League Central race.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: After watching a six-run lead disappear, the Chicago White Sox have little time to regroup in a tightening American League Central race. Chicago will look to bounce back Saturday afternoon when it continues a four-game series against the visiting Detroit Tigers. Saturday's game was moved up from its originally scheduled evening start to 2:10 p.m. ET because of expected inclement weather. The White Sox (78-76) fell one game behind Cleveland after squandering an 8-2 lead in Friday's 11-8 loss to the Tigers. The Guardians (79-75) beat the Athletics 5-3 to take sole possession of first place, although Chicago holds the tiebreaker after winning the season series 7-6. Detroit scored nine unanswered runs, including five in the eighth inning. Hao-Yu Lee tied the game with a two-run homer before Dillon Dingler delivered the go-ahead single and Riley Greene followed with a two-run homer. Lee went 4-for-5 with three RBIs and two runs, while Kevin McGonigle finished 2-for-5 with four RBIs. "I knew there was a chance," Lee told Detroit SportsNet of his game-tying homer. "When I actually saw it go out, I just blacked out. I don't know what I said or did." Detroit (73-81) has won seven of its past nine games. Chicago's offense provided plenty of early support Friday. Colson Montgomery ripped a three-run double during a six-run first inning, while Miguel Vargas hit a two-run homer in the third to match Munetaka Murakami for the team lead with 32. "Yeah, it's tough. No way about it," White Sox manager Will Venable said. "Obviously you have a special first inning there and get the lead. Vargy with a nice homer. Just weren't able to get any outs." Saturday's pitching matchup features Detroit right-hander Jackson Jobe (2-2, 3.89 ERA) against Chicago right-hander Sean Burke (9-7, 3.47). Jobe is coming off his strongest outing of the season. He allowed one run on three hits over a career-high 6 1/3 innings Sunday against the Colorado Rockies, walking one and striking out a career-best eight batters. The White Sox enjoyed considerably more success against Jobe on Aug. 14, tagging him for six runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings in a 9-5 Chicago victory. It was Jobe's only appearance against Chicago this season. Jobe is 0-1 with a 6.17 ERA in three career appearances, including two starts, against the White Sox. Burke pitched five innings of relief Monday against Cleveland, allowing one unearned run on four hits with two walks and four strikeouts in Chicago's 7-3 victory. In two starts against Detroit this season, Burke has allowed five runs over 9 2/3 innings. He is 1-0 with a 2.91 ERA in four career starts against the Tigers. Chicago right fielder Tristan Peters is day-to-day with a left shoulder/rib contusion after crashing into the wall while pursuing McGonigle's fifth-inning triple Friday. "I feel all right," Peters said. "We'll see how it feels (on Saturday). Just really sore right now." --Field Level Media

item.title: IMF tells EU ministers AI could boost growth but increase economic strains
item.description: Artificial intelligence could lift European productivity by about 1% over five years, but risks widening inequality, straining power networks and increasing dependence on foreign technology unless governments deepen economic integration, an International Monetary Fund paper said.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence could lift European productivity by about 1% over five years, but risks widening inequality, straining power networks and increasing dependence on foreign technology unless governments deepen economic integration, an International Monetary Fund paper said. The background note, prepared for an informal meeting of European Union finance ministers in Dublin on September 18-19, said the benefits and costs of AI were likely to be distributed unevenly across countries, regions and workers. It said completing the EU single market would help spread AI adoption and its gains more evenly across the 27-nation bloc. The paper echoes concerns raised by former European Central Bank President Mario Draghi and the European Commission that Europe's fragmented capital, labour and energy markets are holding back investment and innovation. The IMF estimated that around 60% of workers in advanced European economies are employed in occupations highly exposed to AI. While some could become more productive through AI tools, others faced displacement as routine tasks become automated, it said, particularly in jobs where AI is more likely to replace labour than complement it. The paper said Europe's data centres already consume roughly 3% of the continent's electricity and that demand would rise sharply as AI use expands. Major technology hubs such as Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris and Dublin are among the areas most exposed, with data-centre clusters already putting pressure on local power networks. To address that, the EU should invest in cross-border grid infrastructure and deepen integration of the European energy market, the IMF said. The paper also warned that Europe risks developing another strategic dependency because the US and China dominate the development of AI models. It said Europe would need significant investment in its own AI industry to avoid becoming reliant on foreign technology. AI's gains are also likely to be unevenly distributed across and within the EU, the paper said. More advanced economies are expected to benefit disproportionately because they are better prepared for and more exposed to the technology. (This story has been refiled to fix a typo in paragraph 7.)

item.title: Canada optimistic about concluding trade talks with India by year-end, minister says
item.description: Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal
item.content:encoded: Canada is optimistic about concluding negotiations on a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) with India by year-end, the country's minister for international trade said on Saturday. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney had previously said during a trip to New Delhi in March that the two countries would aim to agree a [USN:L1N3ZQ08U TEXT:"free trade pact"] by the end of the year. "I'm feeling very, very optimistic and energetic that we can get it done in the coming months," Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu told Reuters in an interview during a visit to India's financial capital Mumbai. Indian trade negotiators are expected to be in Canada next month and leaders from the two countries are likely to meet on the sidelines of the G-20 gathering in December, Sidhu said. One main area of discussion is the energy sector. A Shell-led (SHEL.L) [USN:L6N45913X TEXT:"LNG export facility"] launched in Canada last year and the country has five more projects in various phases of development. "We're having conversations with Indian firms on how they can access those projects, but also how they can invest and secure supply in those projects," Sidhu said, declining to share further details. Beyond liquefied natural gas, both countries are looking to expand cooperation in nuclear energy, where India is looking to significantly [USN:L1N44B0NC TEXT:"boost capacity"]. "Canada has a long history in the nuclear industry, and I do see a lot of benefit for Canadian companies and industries to help build up a supply chain here in India," Sidhu said. Sidhu said, without giving any further details, that a number of large Indian business houses from Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) to Mahindra and Mahindra (MAHM.NS) and the JSW Group are exploring investments in critical mineral projects in Canada as a way to secure supply chains. Companies are looking at ways to make co-investments as supply chains are getting weaponised, he said.
